title: The RICE math that kills your highest-impact feature
description:
In this lesson's worked example, SSO support scores the maximum on per-user impact and still loses the priority fight. We walk the actual RICE numbers: how low reach and high effort drag a strong bet below a small, cheap fix that reaches everyone. Then the caveat that matters -- RICE informs the call, it doesn't make it.

Source lesson(s):
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/04-prioritization-basics/

#Shorts

beats.narration: The feature with the highest impact on every user it touched lost the priority fight. Here's the RICE math that killed it.
SSO scores a three out of three on impact, the max. But it reaches only forty accounts a quarter and costs two person-months. RICE score: sixty.
A small fix, letting users change their digest email frequency, scores just a two on impact. But it reaches eight hundred a quarter and takes half a month. Score: over two thousand five hundred.
Reach times impact times confidence, divided by effort. A big win for a few people can't beat a modest win for everyone, cheaply.

display.heading: RICE = (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort
display.subheading: Low reach plus high effort sinks a high-impact bet

beats.narration: That's the counter-intuitive result RICE exists to surface. SSO might still ship if it unblocks a specific large deal. The score informs the call, it doesn't make it.

display.heading: RICE informs the decision -- it doesn't replace judgment
display.subheading: A strategic bet can still win despite a low score

beats.narration: Full breakdown, with the scoring tables, is in the lesson.
